lines.trans: Bye, guys, I am flying to Sochi to go skiing!
Vitya, how is my festive dinner coming along?
Almost ready, but one problem has come up for us.
Your white truffle will not be enough for two dishes.
Unfortunately, it turned out to be quite hollow inside.
Let me quickly cook something else for you?
Then we will do this—we will stretch out the intrigue nicely!
Let Eleonora eat the truffle dish alone first.
And I will make a grand appearance at the table a bit later!
Right when they serve your signature dessert.
And are you completely sure that she likes sweets?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will prepare', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Держи смирно, Витя, завтра вечером приготовишь для неё!
examples.trans: Hold it carefully, Vitya, tomorrow evening you will cook it for her!

examples.trans: I made a cake.

examples.text: Мама приготовила вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А почему тогда на пальце обручальное кольцо?

meanings.en: to appear, to show up, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'явиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to appear, to show up', paired with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!

examples.text: У нас появилась хорошая идея.
examples.trans: We came up with a good idea.

examples.text: Я тебе серьёзно говорю. Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously. Let him just show up here one more time!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You certainly cannot buy brains with daddy's money!

examples.trans: It just will not come off at all, it is completely stuck!

examples.text: Мне срочно нужна большая ваза с водой.
examples.trans: I urgently need a large vase with water.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И за столом сразу открою ей все карты!

examples.text: А я эффектно появлюсь за столиком чуть позже!
examples.trans: And I will make a grand appearance at the table a bit later!

examples.text: Отлично, цветы на столе, всё точно на месте!
examples.trans: Great, the flowers are on the table, everything is right in place!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'almost, nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я эффектно появлюсь за столиком чуть позже!
examples.trans: And I will make a grand appearance at the table a bit later!

examples.text: Ничего, я из-за них сам чуть с парашютом не прыгнул!
examples.trans: It is fine, because of them I almost jumped with a parachute myself!

examples.text: Я чуть с парашютом не прыгнул!
examples.trans: I almost jumped with a parachute!
